findings.issue: `hasDerivAt_fdBoundary_of_ne` — the contour is differentiable off the three corner parameters — is a pure derivative fact about `fdBoundary`, depending on no winding theory. Deriv.lean is its canonical home: it is exactly the missing member of the `hasDerivAt_fdBoundary_of_lt_one` … `_of_gt_four` family advertised in that file's module docstring ("away from the segment-junction parameters the contour itself differentiates like its active segment"), and it is assembled here purely from those four lemmas. Any later FTC-over-the-whole-contour argument needs it and will re-derive it.

findings.evidence: Basic.lean:396 `injOn_fdBoundary_arc`, :367 `eqOn_fdBoundary_arc`, :486 `im_fdBoundary_arc_le`, :618 `norm_fdBoundary_arc` — the arc parameterization facts; NonCorner.lean:697-718 uses only `eqOn_fdBoundary_arc` and `Complex.arg`. Containment.lean:20-22 states the geometry/winding separation rationale.
findings.fix: Move both to `FundamentalDomainBoundary/Basic.lean` beside `injOn_fdBoundary_arc` (or to Containment.lean, whose stated purpose is contour geometry usable without importing winding theory) and make them public.
findings.issue: `exists_arc_param` (with its helper `arg_mem_Ioo`, line 676) is the surjectivity of the arc parameterization onto the open unit arc — pure contour geometry, independent of winding, and the direct companion of `injOn_fdBoundary_arc` in Basic.lean. Keeping it private in a winding-value file hides a basic parameterization fact that the forthcoming valence restatement (mapping boundary divisor points to parameters) will need.

summary: Placement of the new file, the module deletions and all imports are correct, but two general contour facts are buried as private lemmas in the winding-value file instead of their canonical earlier homes (Deriv.lean and Basic.lean).
